rv.q: Without more spark behind Joe Mantello's handsomely imagined lowlife of a production, the Chicago darkness starts to feel more dull than glittery.
But it might just as easily be evidence of a production in mourning for its own lifelessness.
Risch is never less than professional, but his costars must struggle to compensate for his shortcomings in this tricky story.
But what this Pal Joey communicates is that any new libretto, however efficient it might be, will be spinning in place without a proper sense of direction.

cn.t: This long-awaited revival disappoints critics with joyless direction and an understudy lead who can't fill the shoes of his predecessors, resulting in a production that feels more like dress-up than gritty, sophisticated pulp fiction.

vs.sum: The legendary former nightclub retains a distinctive atmosphere even in its theatrical configuration. However, comfort is among the worst on Broadway — the rear mezzanine is extremely steep with limited guardrails and tight legroom throughout both levels.

acc.note: No elevator to Mezzanine. 10 induction loops. 81 assistive listening devices. Orchestra wheelchair seating.
